universal_rules: Treat every firearm as if it's loaded, always.
Never point the muzzle at anything you're not willing to destroy.
Keep your finger off the trigger until your sights are on target and you've decided to fire.
Know your target and what's beyond it.
universal_storage: Store unloaded, locked, with ammunition stored separately when not in use.

categories.title: Semi-Automatic Handgun (9mm/.45 platforms)
safe_handling_checklist: Rack slide and visually + physically check chamber is empty
Point muzzle in a safe direction throughout
disassembly_steps: Remove magazine
Rack to clear chamber
Lock slide back
Rotate takedown lever
Ease slide forward off frame
Remove recoil spring and barrel
cleaning_steps: Bore snake or rod front-to-back through barrel
Solvent on bore brush, several passes
Wipe rails and frame
Light oil on rails and barrel exterior
reassembly_and_function_check: Reverse disassembly order
Function-check: trigger reset, safety engage
Reinsert magazine only after check complete
categories.storage_notes: Locked case, unloaded, ammunition stored separately.

categories.title: Pump-Action Shotgun (12ga/20ga)
safe_handling_checklist: Open action, visually + physically check chamber and magazine tube are empty
disassembly_steps: Remove magazine cap
Slide barrel off
Separate forend/pump assembly per manufacturer steps
cleaning_steps: Bore snake through barrel
Clean magazine tube
Wipe action bars
Light oil on moving parts, avoid over-oiling near chamber
reassembly_and_function_check: Reassemble in reverse order
Function check
Store unloaded and locked
categories.storage_notes: Locked case, unloaded, ammunition stored separately.

categories.title: Bolt-Action Rifle (.22LR through common hunting calibers)
safe_handling_checklist: Open bolt and lock rearward to visually confirm chamber is empty
Physically check chamber and feed with a finger sweep if uncertain
Remove detachable magazine (if equipped) before any cleaning steps
Point muzzle in a safe direction throughout
disassembly_steps: Remove bolt by pulling the bolt release/catch and sliding bolt out the rear
Remove magazine (detachable) or ensure internal magazine is empty
Most cleaning does not require removing barrel from stock — do so only if your specific model's manual calls for it
cleaning_steps: Run bore snake or patch-and-rod front-to-back through the barrel
Apply solvent to a bore brush, scrub several passes, follow with dry patches until they come out clean
Wipe down bolt body and lugs, apply a light film of oil to bolt lugs and rails
Wipe exterior metal surfaces with a lightly oiled cloth
reassembly_and_function_check: Reinsert bolt, cycle action several times to confirm smooth operation
Test trigger and safety engagement with chamber empty before storing
Reinsert magazine last, after function check is complete
categories.storage_notes: Store unloaded, action open or bolt removed if possible, in a locked cabinet or safe. Ammunition stored separately.

categories.title: Revolver (.22 through common defensive/hunting calibers)
safe_handling_checklist: Open cylinder and visually check every chamber is empty
Point muzzle in a safe direction while checking
Do not close cylinder until cleaning/inspection is complete
disassembly_steps: Most revolvers do not require full disassembly for routine cleaning — cylinder swings out for access
Do not attempt to remove the sideplate or internal lockwork — this is gunsmith-level work, not routine maintenance
For models with removable grips, grips may be taken off for a more thorough wipe-down
cleaning_steps: Clean each chamber individually with a bore brush and solvent, followed by dry patches
Clean the barrel front-to-back same as chamber cleaning
Clean the forcing cone (front of frame where barrel meets cylinder) — this area builds up carbon quickly
Wipe down the exterior of the cylinder face and frame
Apply a light film of oil to the crane/yoke pivot point and cylinder exterior
reassembly_and_function_check: Close cylinder gently, do not snap it shut
Test trigger pull and cylinder rotation with chamber empty
Confirm cylinder locks up tight with no excess play before storing
categories.storage_notes: Store unloaded, cylinder closed but not loaded, in a locked container. Ammunition stored separately.

categories.title: Break-Action Shotgun (Single or Double Barrel)
safe_handling_checklist: Break the action open — this is the single most reliable visual safety check for this platform
Visually and physically confirm both chambers (or single chamber) are empty
Keep action open any time the gun is not actively being fired
disassembly_steps: Remove forend by releasing the forend latch
Separate barrel(s) from the receiver by opening the action fully and lifting the barrel away
This is typically the full extent of routine disassembly needed for cleaning
cleaning_steps: Run a bore snake or patch-and-rod through each barrel front-to-back
Clean the chamber end of each barrel and the breech face on the receiver where the barrels seat
Wipe extractors/ejectors and apply a light film of oil
Wipe down exterior metal and hinge pin with a lightly oiled cloth
reassembly_and_function_check: Reattach barrel(s) to receiver, then reattach forend
Cycle the action open and closed to confirm smooth operation
Test trigger(s) with action closed and chamber(s) empty before storing
categories.storage_notes: Store unloaded with action open when possible, in a locked case. Ammunition stored separately.

categories.title: Semi-Automatic Rifle (AR-Platform and similar)
safe_handling_checklist: Lock bolt/charging handle rearward and visually + physically check chamber is empty
Point muzzle in a safe direction throughout disassembly
disassembly_steps: Push out takedown and pivot pins to separate upper and lower receiver
Remove charging handle and bolt carrier group (BCG) from the upper receiver
Disassemble BCG: remove firing pin retaining pin, firing pin, cam pin, then rotate and lift out the bolt
Do not remove the gas rings or attempt trigger group disassembly — this goes beyond routine cleaning
cleaning_steps: Clean the bore front-to-back (or chamber-to-muzzle using a bore guide) with solvent and brush, then dry patches
Clean carbon buildup from the bolt tail, bolt lugs, and inside the carrier key using a nylon brush
Clean the chamber with a chamber brush
Wipe down the inside of the upper receiver and buffer tube area
Apply oil to bolt lugs, cam pin, and rails — this platform generally runs best wet, not dry
reassembly_and_function_check: Reassemble BCG in reverse order, confirm cam pin and firing pin retaining pin are fully seated
Reinsert BCG and charging handle into upper receiver
Rejoin upper and lower receivers, replace takedown/pivot pins
Charge the action and test trigger reset with chamber empty before storing
Reinsert magazine only after function check is complete
categories.storage_notes: Store unloaded, magazine removed, bolt closed or open per your safe's configuration, in a locked safe or cabinet. Ammunition stored separately.
